blocks.text: Some traits are not sex-linked, because their alleles are not on the sex chromosomes, but they still occur in different ratios in males and females. There are two categories of such traits.

The genes of sex-limited traits are present in both sexes but are expressed in only one, because of anatomical or hormonal differences. Both male and female sheep carry the genes for horn development, but they are expressed only in males; the genes for milk production are in both male and female mammals but are expressed only in females; and the genes for beard growth in humans are expressed only in males. Similarly the genes for prostate cancer are expressed only in males and those for ovarian cancer only in females, although both sexes carry them.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Sex-limited genes are responsible for sexual dimorphism: the phenotypic differences between males and females of the same species.

In sex-influenced traits the same gene is expressed differently in each sex: the alleles are dominant in one sex and recessive in the other, because of hormonal differences. In humans the amount of body hair and baldness are sex-influenced. The baldness allele is dominant in men but recessive in women.

blocks.caption: Baldness as a sex-influenced trait (B is the baldness allele)

blocks.title: A note on the symbols
blocks.text: The book writes that a man is bald when BB or Bb, and a woman only 'when she inherits two recessive alleles (bb)'. With B as the baldness allele, which the book says is recessive in women, a woman needs two baldness alleles, that is BB, to be bald; the printed 'bb' is read this way, and the table uses it.

blocks.title: For information: genetics today
blocks.text: Genetics is now an applied, practical science: DNA sequencing and genetic engineering let researchers manipulate genes; the completed Human Genome Project has deepened understanding of the genetic basis of diseases and traits; and genetics helps doctors diagnose and treat patients according to their genetic profiles.

blocks.prompt: How does a sex-limited trait differ from a sex-influenced trait?
blocks.explanation: A sex-limited trait is expressed in only one sex (horns in rams, milk in females). A sex-influenced trait shows in both sexes but its allele is dominant in one and recessive in the other (baldness).

items: Neither kind is sex-linked: the genes are on autosomes.
Sex-limited: expressed in one sex only (horns, milk, beard).
Sex-influenced: dominant in one sex, recessive in the other (baldness).
